results.title: Finite-additive Gaussian anti-concentration
results.target: P(Y+Z∈I)≤L/√(2πv) under the specified finite-additive independence contract.
results.input_contract: Foundational article §§3–5; independent review §§1–2, including interval endpoints, sum-event measurability and ordinary real-valued probability.
assumptions: One normalized nonnegative ordinary real-valued finitely additive probability on an event algebra containing every used interval, tail, rectangle and sum event.
Y and Z are rectangle-independent at the stated event scope; Z has an ordinary centred Gaussian marginal with variance v>0.
For history application, all arbitrarily long finite blocks bind the same terminal state and law; their Gaussian variances diverge.
results.conclusion: For bounded interval I of length L, P(Y+Z∈I)≤L/√(2πv); the sharper bound is 2Φ(L/(2√v))−1. Hence fresh Gaussian blocks of arbitrarily large variance force each bounded terminal interval to have probability zero.
limitations: Tightness of Y and joint countable additivity are not required; the Gaussian marginal supplies the tail estimate.
Mutual iid noise does not imply independence of the earlier state from its future innovation block.
The ordinary real limit step is not automatically transferable to non-Archimedean values.
results.operational_model: Ordinary finitely additive probability with explicit Gaussian marginal and event domain.
results.origin_status: These are ordinary written mathematics and model-assisted checks. No new Lean kernel certification is claimed.
results.residual_scope: No formal implementation, actual productive-support identification, metaphysical realisability, normative adoption, empirical replication or specialist/novelty warrant; original obligations retain their declared scopes.

assumptions: The entire noise marginal Q is the ordinary countably additive iid Gaussian law; all recurrences hold pointwise.
A free nonprincipal ultrafilter is fixed once for all Borel events; finite additivity is preserved through scalar ultralimits.
Uniform reanchoring comparison is over the common full Borel event domain.
results.conclusion: The law μ is normalized real-valued and finitely additive, retains full past/future rectangle independence and the entire noise marginal, is stationary and spatially translation-invariant, and gives every bounded position interval mass zero although every sample position is finite.

Probability consistency does not establish physical or metaphysical possibility or productive causal direction.
Anchored countably additive paths with X_0=0 retain iid noise but fail state/future freshness; stable AR(1) and deterministic translation are distinct positive controls.

assumptions: P_n and independent benchmark Q_n share the specified state/noise marginals and a common measurable pair-event domain.

Q_n satisfies the concentration assumptions; full-Borel finitely additive benchmark construction has the stated integration order.

A realized value or pointwise expanding-search termination does not establish positive capture at a fixed finite budget.

Bounded interval I has positive length L and fixed capture mass p; information is D(P_n||P_Y⊗P_S).

A finite program description, quantized readout or instantaneous controller state is not automatically a complete mediator.
Uncontrolled side information contributes I(U_n;S_n); no actual physical capacity or original-coordinator existence is established.

assumptions: Accepted Ω=R×R^Z path law and pointwise recurrence.
For each j∈J put Δ_j=a_j−ξ_j and adjust anchor by Σ_{j∈J,j<0}Δ_j.
J is finite and targets/values are prescribed, not adaptive or future-dependent.
results.conclusion: The Borel replacement map gives X′_t−X_t=Σ_{j∈J,j<t}Δ_j. Prehistory through min J stays fixed, all recurrences hold, distinct-time replacements commute, and pushforward preserves finite additivity, unmodified Gaussian noise and full transformed past/future factorisation.

results.title: Completed reports, two-trade loss and forecast limits
results.target: The completed two-trade policy is uniformly dominated; bounded capture and dynamic-policy routes have different conclusions.
results.input_contract: Bounded access §§5–10, read with final observation-route clarification; A has probability 1/2, R=N on A and geometric K on Aᶜ.
assumptions: Each positive report H_n={R=n} has μ(H_n)=2^{−n}/2 and μ(A|H_n)=0; same operative probability and information state.
Report access, preserved ticket transfer, exact timing/no extra information and action-guidance policy are warranted separately.
Two-trade parameter 0<ε<1/4; trade one buys at 1/2−ε and trade two resells the same ticket at ε.
results.conclusion: The completed policy loses −1/2+2ε in every outcome and abstention dominates it. Exact-report posterior forecasting has prior quadratic loss 1/2 versus constant prior 1/4. At deadline m the residual D_m has posterior 1/(2−Q_m) and expected loss (1−Q_m)/[2(2−Q_m)], so finite truncations do not inherit completed sure loss.
limitations: The history, reporter and losing behavior remain mathematically consistent; this is a dominated-policy result, not impossibility of the support architecture.
The agent may abstain, precommit, revise its model or reject an unwarranted service assumption; an original-support argument must address these rational responses.
Outright resale or buyback locks loss at report time; later physical settlement need not be an extra executed stage, while warranted ticket value/transfer conditions remain required.

results.input_contract: Integer total report protocol §§1–6 and final clarification; private input sign and unary magnitude tape 1^{|x|}0, fixed bounded padded rounds.
assumptions: Accepted finitely additive integer ±1 path law supplies finite anchor input x and existing iid sign bits.
Input representation, sign, length/loading time and private coin bits are hidden from the trader; the public clock/silence/pulse transcript is exact.
N=1+|X_0|, K*=min(first later head,N), R=N on A and K* on Aᶜ; maintained channel/opportunities and input supply are separate assumptions.
results.conclusion: Every valid finite input and every tape, including all tails, reports in R≤N<∞ rounds. The transducer needs fixed finite control plus supplied tape; no actual run requires infinite working memory. Input/channel/clock repertoires remain unbounded across runs.
No sampler for μ, physical implementation, Gaussian exact-real acquisition algorithm, actual indefinite service or canonical adoption is provided.
